column1: # Per-file real macOS bats wall time (seconds), used by shard-tests.sh to
# weight the CI partition by measured cost instead of @test count (#1243).
# @test count is a loose, occasionally blind proxy for a file's real cost:
# a file whose time is almost entirely waiting (background processes, poll
# loops) can carry a tiny count while dominating its shard's wall clock, and
# a file that is merely large in @test count is not necessarily slow. This
# table sidesteps the proxy by using each file's own measured time directly.
# MEASURED AGAINST: GitHub Actions run 36622150859 (tests.yml bats job,
# macos-latest, 5 shards, 2026-09-29; the full-suite PR run of #1519, whose
# head was main plus a test-only change to test_codex_bridge_launcher.bats).
# Every shard in that run completed, so every file below has a real file_end
# record -- summed from the run's 5 bats-timings-macos-latest-* artifacts
# (file_end rows only, macOS only). All 127 test files are present.
# WHY THIS REFRESH: two rows had gone wrong in a way that broke the
# partition. test_ext_tool_jev_handle.bats (605s, the heaviest file in the
# suite) had no row at all and was estimated at the table average, and
# test_watch.bats still carried its quarantined 2s although it has run for
# real since it was unquarantined (216s now). A new test file shifted the
# partition so that both landed on one macOS shard, which then hit the
# test_safe_poke_draft.bats had no row either and are added here.
# (2026-09-14). See git history for the reasoning recorded with each.
# A file with no row here (renamed, or added after this measurement) is
# estimated at this table's own average seconds/file by shard-tests.sh,
# never treated as zero-cost or dropped from the partition -- coverage does
# not depend on this table being current. tests/test_ci_sharding.bats's
# balance-ratio assertion checks the computed partition against THIS
# table's own numbers, not against a live run, so it cannot detect this
# table drifting out of sync with reality -- only a human noticing a real
# run's shard skew (as happened here) triggers a refresh. Refresh by
# re-running this extraction against a green run's bats-timings artifacts.
# PROVISIONAL DELIVERY WEIGHTS (2026-10-03): the nine new delivery suites
# below use isolated Linux measurements or enclosing-gate upper bounds.
# These are scheduling estimates, NOT macOS file_end measurements. Replace
# them with per-file values from the next completed macOS CI timing artifacts.
# Isolated Linux seconds, rounded up: antigravity_claims 67.601,
# Conservative enclosing-gate seconds, rounded up: antigravity_claims_bytes
# claims + bytes); delivery_claims and delivery_readers each 278.530
# This avoids assigning long new suites the unrelated table-average cost.
# Columns: basename<TAB>seconds. Sorted by basename for a legible diff.
